{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research, specifically Understand Anything's "diff impact analysis that shows what a given change touches". STILL OPEN.

THE IDEA: reflow2's impact analysis runs design-first — add_change_event then propagate_change, seeded by the design node you are about to touch. The survey's tools run it code-first: here is a diff, here is what it touches. Those are opposite directions, and the code-first direction is the one a developer actually has in hand at review time.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, and this was checked rather than assumed: reconcile_artifacts takes observed artifact hashes and returns `propagation_seeds` — "the design nodes the changes land on" — explicitly documented to be fed to propagate_from. So the code-to-design hop is BUILT. The composition is: changed files, to registered artifacts by hash, to REALIZES edges, to capabilities and upward. Nothing is missing in the core.

WHAT IS THEREFORE ACTUALLY OPEN, and it is smaller than the survey makes it sound: (a) nothing computes the hashes from a commit — reflow2 performs no file I/O by design, so a caller must do it, and no caller currently does it from a git diff; (b) the CI gate checks the committed export for drift and open gaps, not "what does this commit touch upstream"; (c) the answer is only as complete as artifact registration, and an unregistered file lands on nothing at all, which would read as "this change is safe" rather than "this change is unmapped". That last one is the real risk and it is the same failure mode as the release-manifest problem: silence that looks like a pass.

WHAT IS CHEAP: a driver script over `git diff --name-only` plus hashing, calling reconcile_artifacts then propagate_from. That is wiring, in the same family as tools/reflow2_check.py, and needs no core change.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a per-commit blast radius is only as trustworthy as REALIZES coverage, and an incomplete golden thread turns it into a confident understatement — which is worse than no answer, because a reviewer will believe it. If this is built, the honest version must report unmapped files as UNMAPPED and loudly, not fold them into a clean result. The existing unrealized_capability gap is the design-side half of that problem; this is the artifact-side half and there may be nothing that detects it.","name":"OPEN — should a git diff be a direct input to impact analysis, given reconcile_artifacts already returns propagation_seeds and nothing drives it from a commit?","rationale":"Recorded as an idea rather than a gap because the machinery it asks for already exists and only the driver is absent, which makes it a small increment rather than a design question — except for the unmapped-file silence, which is a design question and is the reason this is worth a node at all.","status":"accepted"}
